texts.orig: Individualized Development Plan (IDP)
texts.text: Individualized Development Plan (IDP)

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The Faculty of Graduate Studies' IDP is a tool to assist graduate students, like you, to identify and develop your goals during your studies. This IDP is an abridged version that has been designed for graduate students who prefer a more streamlined option compared to the full IDP based on their individual preferences.
texts.text: The Faculty of Graduate Studies' IDP is a tool to assist graduate students, like you, to identify and develop your goals during your studies. This IDP is an abridged version that has been designed for graduate students who prefer a more streamlined option compared to the full IDP based on their individual preferences.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: When creating an IDP, with the help of a mentor, you can enhance your professional growth and skills by:
texts.text: When creating an IDP, with the help of a mentor, you can enhance your professional growth and skills by:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig:  Setting and communicating goals related to teaching, research and/or professional development with your supervisor, faculty colleagues or other mentors
texts.text:  Setting and communicating goals related to teaching, research and/or professional development with your supervisor, faculty colleagues or other mentors

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig:  Identifying ways to learn or improve your competencies to be used during your graduate work and within professional spaces
texts.text:  Identifying ways to learn or improve your competencies to be used during your graduate work and within professional spaces

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig:  Identifying your strengths, talents and passions, as well as opportunities to use them during your studies and in your future professional life while building an effective support network
texts.text:  Identifying your strengths, talents and passions, as well as opportunities to use them during your studies and in your future professional life while building an effective support network

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The development of an IDP is a cyclical process. You are encouraged to revisit it over the course of your program of study as interests and long-term goals evolve. The five steps in working with the IDP are as follows:
texts.text: The development of an IDP is a cyclical process. You are encouraged to revisit it over the course of your program of study as interests and long-term goals evolve. The five steps in working with the IDP are as follows:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: 1. Self-Assessment/Reflection: looking back while planning for the future
texts.text: Self-Assessment/Reflection: looking back while planning for the future

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: 2. Setting Goals: clarifying the knowledge and skills you need
texts.text: Setting Goals: clarifying the knowledge and skills you need

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: 3. Exploring Opportunities: developing a strategy for realizing your plan
texts.text: Exploring Opportunities: developing a strategy for realizing your plan

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: 4. Engagement: acting on your plan to achieve your goals
texts.text: Engagement: acting on your plan to achieve your goals

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: 5. Check-in: revisit to update your goals and engagement activities
texts.text: Check-in: revisit to update your goals and engagement activities

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Further information, resources and relevant contact information can be found on the Individualized Development Plan (IDP) webpage.
texts.text: Further information, resources and relevant contact information can be found on the Individualized Development Plan (IDP) webpage.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Keeping your self-assessment/reflection in mind, situate your current portfolio (e.g., achievements and successes), plan out goals and next steps, and then revisit the IDP to describe and identify the skills that your engagement helped to develop.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: 1. Refer to your resume/CV when reflecting on your current portfolio. You do not have to list everything; rather, focus on the main points that give a sense of your work thus far. These points can also be useful when writing a cover letter or when providing a reference with a summary of your experience and involvement.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: 2. Graduate students are strongly encouraged to view all professional skills opportunities and resources at York University - organized under the six competency areas of the IDP - on the Graduate and Postdoctoral Professional Skills (GPPS) webpage. The webpage includes a list of resources that can be identified as next steps and opportunities.

texts.orig: 3. Use the IDP Examples to get a sense of how to frame and set goals, next steps, and skills. It can also be helpful to speak with a mentor (who may be your Supervisor and Graduate Program Director, for example) to get further support and to revise your plans based on your short-term and long-term goals.
